text:
maria: Heads up — we're planning a breaking change to the SDK auth header (moving from `X-Redwood-Auth` -> `Authorization: Bearer`) that will affect marketplace listings and partner integrations. Want to align on a compatibility gate and partner outreach timeline.

aj: Thanks — rough timeline? We should avoid landing near the next marketplace sync on Apr 12.

maria: Targeting an opt-in canary the week of Apr 20, public rollout May 5, full deprecation window 90 days after rollout. Open to shifting if partners need longer.

kevin: For hardware partners with on-prem installs, 90d seems tight. Can we do a 180d deprecation window or a longer dual-support phase for Dedicated/private customers?

maria: We can add a dual-support flag. Proposal: SDK v3.x supports both headers, v4.0 defaults to `Authorization`. v3.x will get backported security fixes during the window.

ellie: From comms: need a joint announcement plan for marketplace partners and SI integrators. We should surface migration steps and a one-line snippet they can paste.

maria: Agreed. Draft snippet: "Important: Redwood SDK authentication header will change in May. Please migrate to `Authorization: Bearer <token>` by July 5 to avoid disruption. See migration guide: <link>" Thoughts?

sam-partner: Sam (CloudCo) — our marketplace listing uses the older header in the installer. We can do the canary but need at least 120 days before forced migration for enterprise customers. Also request a patch release for our billing agent.

aj: Can we accommodate 120d for marketplace vendor installs? We can extend the deprecation window for Marketplace images/channel partners while keeping shorter window for hosted API customers.

kevin: Ops note: we'll need a feature-flag gated rollout on infra side. Suggest `auth-header-compat` feature flag with default ON for 120d, then ramp down. Add logs that emit `legacy-auth: true` when old header used so partners can see usage.

maria: Good — also need DevEx to add a one-line migration CLI: `rw migrate-auth --to authorization` to update local installs. Ellie, can docs + snippet + CLI be ready before Apr 20 canary?

ellie: I'll own docs + partner-facing checklist. CLI pinged to @aj for a minimal shim. ETA Apr 15.

aj: I'll land the shim and the flag. Plan: create branch `compat/auth-header-2026` and open PRs this week.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot created branch compat/auth-header-2026 and CI pipeline started — see: https://ci.redwood/example/compat-auth-2026

maria: Next steps: 1) finalize timeline and announce to partners on Apr 1 (pre-notice) 2) Apr 15 docs + migration CLI ready 3) Apr 20 canary with selected partners 4) May 5 public opt-in rollout 5) Sep 2 forced switch for marketplace images (120d) unless exceptions requested. Anyone object?

sam-partner: Requesting a partner exception process in the announcement (support ticket link and account manager contact). We'll share that with our enterprise customers.

maria: Yes — we'll include a partner exception form and AM escalation. I'll draft the announcement and send to this channel for review.

kevin: Also, add a compatibility test to the SDK contract tests that fails build if both headers are missing. That will help partners catch regressions.

aj: Will add the test in CI.

ellie: I'll prepare an FAQ: how to detect legacy header usage (log filters), how to roll back, and sample nginx patch for on-prem images.

maria: Great — thanks all. I'll post the draft announcement here by EOD tomorrow for review.

sam-partner: Thanks — we'll queue this with our PM and get initial feedback by Apr 5.

kevin: One more ask — can we add a migration telemetry event `auth.migrated` that partners can opt into so we can track uptake?

maria: Yes, opt-in telemetry via a partner consent flag. Add to docs.

aj: Noted. I'll wire the telemetry hook into the shim.

maria: Closing loop — draft announcement posted (link: <internal doc link>). Please add comments. We will not merge any breaking change without partner sign-off for marketplace-provisioned images.
